A person opens a paperback and lays the blue banknotes from the table between its pages. They close the book with part of the money still protruding and lift it. Holding the black handbag open by a strap, the person lowers the book toward its opening, reaches inside, and then folds the top down and presses the bag flat.

A woman lifts the left of two inverted blue cups to show an empty spot, then raises the right cup to reveal a small white ball. After covering the ball, she slides the cups around with both hands. The left cup is lifted to expose the ball in its new position and lowered again; a final lift of the right cup shows it is empty before both cups return to the counter.

A person lifts three inverted white cups in turn, revealing a small pale blue ball beneath the middle cup and empty spaces under the outer cups, then covers them again. They slide and exchange the cups with both hands before returning them to a row. They lift each cup again, showing the ball under the middle one, and finish with all three inverted.

A person lifts the inverted white-and-gold cups one at a time, showing a red-and-white ball beneath the cup farther from the camera. They cover it and slide the cups around each other on the black counter. After the shuffle, the back cup reveals an empty space and the front cup reveals the ball; they lower both cups again.

A person lifts each of two inverted yellow cups, showing empty space beneath the left cup and a small white bottle beneath the right, then covers both positions again. They slide the cups forward and closer together on the counter. They repeat the reveals in the same order, with the bottle still beneath the right cup, and finish with both cups inverted.

A person lifts three upside-down white cups one at a time, showing a small dark object beneath the cup on the right. They put the cups down and slide them around with both hands. After rearranging them, they lift the cups again, revealing the object under the middle cup before returning all three to an inverted row.

A seated person brings a shallow rectangular dish onto the dark round table and sets it on the right. They reach off to the left for a translucent plastic bowl and place it beside the dish. They add a round metal bowl farther left and adjust it slightly, leaving all three containers open and arranged side by side.

A person picks up a dark rectangular lid and fits it onto the purple food container at the front of the table. They place the orange round lid over the small orange tub and press it down. They then lift the bright pink drinking lid, position it on the purple handled cup, and turn it while steadying the cup with their other hand.

A person places an orange near the back of a round red table, then sets a clear drinking glass to its right. They add a small white bowl in front of the orange and stand a tall pink bottle beside the glass. Finally, they place a small labeled bottle behind the bowl, leaving the objects spaced across the tabletop.

A person places a translucent purple cup upright near the back of the round table. They add a second cup in front of it, turning this one upside down, then set a third cup upright closer to the front edge. The cups form a short diagonal row beside the small roll of tape.

A person picks up the flat turquoise lid and lays it across the translucent pitcher's opening. They set the round green lid at an angle on top of the square blue container, then place the small blue cap on the clear water bottle. The tea box, scissors and pens remain spread across the front of the table.

A person lifts the middle gray hardback and stacks it on the book to the left, squaring their edges. They take the folded newspaper from behind the books and lay it across the stack. They then lift the remaining hardback from the front right and place it on top, leaving the newspaper sandwiched between books as their hands withdraw.

A person gathers the books into a stack on a small table, placing the pale book on top of the red one. They move a black-handled utensil up and down against the top cover. Keeping the utensil in one hand, they lift the white and green hair dryer with the other and turn it above the table.

A person lifts the small book from the cabinet and opens it above the larger book lying underneath. They pick up the pale rectangular slip, lay it between the pages and close the small book. They move it toward the red bag, open the bag’s top and lower their hands at the opening before letting go and stepping back.

A person turns a white-covered paperback and lays it flat in front of them on a black grid-patterned cloth. They lift an orange towel, fold and square it between both hands, then place it on top of the book. A second blue-and-white paperback is lifted from the left and laid over the towel, leaving the wristwatch separate at the front.

The person moves the two small books to the left and rests one end of the thick white book on them to make a slope. They shift the coffee tin to the right of the raised book. Holding a small cork with a dark base, they release it near the raised end, retrieve it near the lower end, and repeat the movement.

A person opens the paperback on the bedside table, briefly spreads its pages, and closes it again. They slide the book back toward the wall and move the pink pen alongside its right edge. They then adjust the knife near the front of the table so its blade points toward the red lamp base; the lamp stays lit beside the glass and metal pan.

A person switches on the white table lamp, lighting the wooden surface, then turns the knife so its blade points to the left. They reach beside the lamp and switch it off. In the dimmer light, they turn the knife again so it points toward the front of the table, then switch the lamp back on.

The person opens a book on the blue storage-box lid and moves a glass of clear liquid onto its pages. They plug the white desk lamp into the wall socket, then adjust the open book beneath the glass. Finally, they press the switch on the lamp cord, and a bright patch of light appears across the pages.

A person runs a hand across the red tablecloth, then places a dark book near the center of the table. They add an upside-down clear cup to its right and lay a green pen on the cover. A small jar with a red lid goes beside the clear cup, and a white mug is placed to the left of the book.

A person reaches beside the red desk lamp and switches it on, lighting the plant and books on the glass table. They lift a book, open it briefly, and close it before returning it to the stack. After switching the lamp off again, they gather the colored markers into their hands and lower them back beside the books.

A person takes the light gray garment from the top of a clothing pile, folds it, and sets it at the front of the table. They fold the white garment with orange and dark stripes and stack it on the gray one, then add folded camouflage clothing on top. Dark gray clothes remain at the back, with the pomegranate, book, and yellow boxes undisturbed on the right.

A person lifts a dark teal garment from a pile on a checked table, folds it, and places it to the left. They fold an orange shirt and add it on top, followed by a red shirt. They then lift the remaining dark patterned sweater, fold it into a compact rectangle, and lay it on the stack, clearing the right side of the table.

A person lifts a gray garment from a pile on a covered table, folds it, and places it near the back. They fold a white garment over it, smoothing the new stack with both hands. Next, they pick up a dark striped shirt, fold it, and add it on top, while a blue garment remains spread separately at the front.

A person folds a dark gray garment at the back of a wooden table and lays it flat near the front left. They fold a beige garment and place it over the first, then add a folded dark shirt with a white graphic on top. They pat the finished stack beside a green glass bowl resting on a book.

A person folds a black garment and smooths it into a flat pile on the left side of the table. They lift the blue garment from the remaining clothes, fold it, and add it to the pile. Next, they fold the mustard-yellow garment over the blue one and finish by placing a small folded gray item on top.

A person turns the yellow toy car to face right and pushes it across the bare tabletop in front of the chopping board. They retrieve it from the right, bring the board forward and slightly left, and hold the car above it. They then release the car onto the board, sending it toward the right edge while the pear on the glass and the loose string remain in place.

A person takes hold of the string attached to a yellow toy car and pulls it across the bare tabletop from left to right. They pick the car up and place it on the stacked wooden boards. Holding the string again, they draw the car across the top board toward its right edge, then lower the string and leave the car there.

A person moves a small green toy car across a worn green tabletop and brings it back beside a white cutting board. They lift the board from the left and set it flat near the center, then place the car on its surface. Keeping their fingers on the toy, they push it from the board left side toward the right edge and continue guiding it there.

A person repositions a white cutting board on a worn green table and puts a bright green toy car near its left end. They lift that end so the car rolls down and off onto the table at the right. They push the car back across the board, adjust the board again and repeat the tilted-board run, leaving the car near the right edge.

A person sets a blue toy car on the wooden table and pulls it to the right using the white string attached to its front. They lift the car, slide a white cutting board into the middle of the table and place the car on it. Pulling the string again brings the car across the board and onto the table at the right.

A man props a large book diagonally against a stack of books, then stands another book upright at the lower end of the slope. He places a small blue paperback near the top and releases it, allowing it to slide down behind the upright book. The paperback is retrieved, reset on the slope and released again, coming to rest partway along the inclined cover.

A person props a red hardcover book at an angle against a stack of books, making a slope behind an upright blue box. They place a red toy car at the raised end and release it down the cover, where it passes behind the box and appears near the front left edge. They retrieve the car and repeat the release from the top of the slope.

A person leans a spiral notebook against a small stack of books to form a ramp, then stands an ornate book upright nearby. They release a clear plastic bottle with a blue cap down the notebook, retrieve it from the right side of the table, and repeat the motion. The sequence ends with another release onto the sloping notebook.

The person moves the two small books to the left and rests one end of the thick white book on them to make a slope. They shift the coffee tin to the right of the raised book. Holding a small cork with a dark base, they release it near the raised end, retrieve it near the lower end, and repeat the movement.

A person arranges three books on a wooden table, leaving one slanted across another and standing the third upright in front of its right end. They release a small orange onto the slanted book; it rolls behind the upright book and emerges on the right. They repeat this twice, then leave the orange beside the books and step away.

A person holds a red block close to the camera with its white A label facing forward, then carries it out of view to the right. An orange-edged block marked B is displayed and removed in the same way. The person finishes by presenting the block labeled C and withdrawing it, while the glass containing an orange knife stays in the middle of the table.

A person lifts a dark glass bottle and turns its label toward the camera before returning it upright. They repeat the display with a clear bottle of yellow oil and set it back beside the first bottle. Finally, they pick up a wrapped pale yellow block, show it close to the camera, and return it to the open wrapping on the table.

A person reaches over a wooden table to display a small beige rectangular piece between their fingers, then withdraws it. They repeat the presentation with two more pale rectangular pieces, holding each above the tabletop before taking it away. Finally, a small purple piece is shown and removed, while the fork and orange object at the far corner stay in place.

Hands display a small wooden bird-shaped carving, a blue fabric strap, and the carving again above a round table, removing each after showing it. A short white adapter cable and a green plastic bottle are then held close to the camera in turn. The carving returns for a final sideways view before it is withdrawn, while the keys and two colored shapes stay on the table.

A person lifts a kitchen knife from beside the table and holds it horizontally between both hands before lowering it out of view. They then present a green writing tool, a yellow one, and a blue one in turn, removing each to the left before showing the next. A lime and black zippered case remain on the fruit-patterned tablecloth throughout.

A person raises a pale paper letter D in front of the camera and lowers it out of view to the left. They display an E, then a K, handling each briefly before taking it away. They finish by holding up a pale triangular cutout and lowering it, while the clear glass, egg carton, and tea box stay on the counter.

Standing behind a counter, a person holds a decorated cutout A upright toward the camera and lowers it out of view. They present B and C next, turning each slightly between their fingers before withdrawing it. After a pause, they show D and then E in the same way, bringing each letter forward above the brown paper before lowering their hand again.

The person picks up a pen and makes marks on a small white sheet on the table. They lift the sheet to show it, then return it beside the pen. Next, they display red letter cutouts one at a time, placing V, C, and U in a row closer to the camera while the cup and green plate stay at the back.

A hand holds a yellow cutout letter D close to the camera and places it flat on the wooden table. The person then displays a letter E cut from multicolored printed card and sets it beside the D. A yellow F is added at the right, leaving the three letters arranged in alphabetical order in front of the small clock, tin, and pink cup.

Standing behind the dark table, the person raises a blue paper E and holds it facing the camera before taking it to the left. They repeat this with an F, a narrow I, and finally an L. Each letter is displayed separately and removed, while the stacked books, white-handled knife, and dark dish stay on the table.

A seated man brings together the open front edges of his blue checked shirt and fastens a button near his waist. His hands move progressively upward, working each button through its hole across his abdomen and chest. He finishes near the collar, then drops his hands toward his lap, leaving the front of the shirt drawn together.

A seated person brings together the lower edges of an open gray shirt and fastens a button near the hem. They work upward with both hands, closing successive buttons across the stomach and chest until only the collar area remains open. After fastening the top button, they release the shirt and lower their hands to their lap.

A seated person pulls the upper edges of a gray shirt together over a beige T shirt and fastens the button near the collar. They continue down the front, using both hands to guide each button through its hole and straighten the fabric. After fastening the lower buttons, they smooth the front and lower their hands with the shirt closed across their torso.

A person brings the two sides of an open, pale checked shirt together near the neck and starts fastening the buttons. Their hands work steadily down the front, pinching each section of fabric together before moving lower. By the end, the front is closed and they are still adjusting the lowest part near the hem.

A person wearing an open blue-and-white shirt brings its lower front edges together and fastens the bottom buttons. They work upward with both hands, closing the shirt across the waist and chest. After fastening the upper buttons near the collar, they lower their hands, leaving the shirt front closed over the black top underneath.

Hands fold the sleeves and sides of a red shirt inward and turn it into a compact rectangle at one end of the table. They fold the gray trousers into a small bundle and place it beside the shirt. After briefly rubbing their palms, the person folds the printed sheet into a smaller rectangle, presses its creases and leaves it beneath the two folded garments.

A seated person lifts a red printed garment, folds it and places it on the table. They fold a dark garment onto it, then add a pale patterned piece to the top of the pile. Finally, they pull a white paper towel toward the front, fold it into a smaller rectangle and smooth it down beside a pair of glasses.

A person folds the sleeves and body of a navy shirt into a rectangle and moves it to the left side of the table. They fold the gray shirt underneath in the same area and stack it over the navy one, then fold the green shorts and add them on top. Finally, they fold a white sheet of paper beside the clothes and press the crease flat.

A person lifts a dark teal garment from a pile on a checked table, folds it, and places it to the left. They fold an orange shirt and add it on top, followed by a red shirt. They then lift the remaining dark patterned sweater, fold it into a compact rectangle, and lay it on the stack, clearing the right side of the table.

A person folds the red printed sheet into a narrow rectangle and leaves it on the left of the small covered table. They lift and fold the cream knitted scarf into a compact bundle at the center. They then fold the white socks together and set them on the right, leaving a row of folded items behind the green vegetable, egg, and spoon.

A woman draws on a white sheet with a blue pen, then raises the page to show a circle on the left and a triangle on the right. She sets the paper down and adds a small colored paper triangle over the left side of the page. A blue plastic cap is placed on the right side, and her hand withdraws with both objects resting on the drawing.

A person uses a blue pen to draw a small circle, a larger circle, and a triangle in a row on white paper, then raises the sheet to show the shapes. After laying it down, they put a red cap over the small circle, a green triangular piece over the larger circle, and a yellow lid over the drawn triangle.

A person uncaps the blue pen and draws on a small white sheet while holding the paper steady. They lay the pen down and lift the sheet close to the camera, showing an outlined triangle beside a square. After returning the paper to the table, they pick up a dark blue square and turquoise triangle and present the colored cutouts together.

A person draws a square and a circle on a white sheet resting over a book, then holds the paper upright to show both outlines. They lay it flat again and place a blue round piece over the left drawing. A red rounded rectangular piece is added over the right drawing, and both pieces remain on the paper beside the marker.

A person removes the cap from a blue pen and draws several lines on a white sheet, holding the paper steady with the other hand. After putting the pen aside, they place a broad white lid on the paper and then a smaller yellow cap in front of it. Both caps remain on the sheet.

A person points to the small paper letter P and briefly shows it on an open palm. They lift the hollow metal tube upright and drop the rough brown object through its upper opening, letting it fall onto the table. They retrieve the object and repeat this twice, then lay the tube on its side beside the object and letter.

A person lowers a small spoon into a white cup, then lifts and tilts the metal kettle above it before returning the kettle to the table. They stir the cup and rearrange the colored plastic letters in front of it. After dipping the spoon into the small metal cup, they return to stirring the white cup while steadying the metal one with the other hand.

A person picks up a dark pen from a wooden table and holds it horizontally between both hands, then puts it back. They repeat the display with a second dark pen before lifting a metal spoon and holding it across their hands in the same way. The spoon is returned beside the pens, while another utensil stays resting across the red container at the left.

The person sets a dark pen on the table, then adds a metal fork beside it. They place a cream-colored pen on the other side of the fork and a small red object nearer the black plant pot. Each item is briefly held above the table before being released, while the tall blue-capped bottle stays upright beside the pot.

A person rests an orange notebook with one end raised on a thick green book, then lays a brown jar on its side at the lower end. They place a thin dark stick across the sloping cover and release it. After reaching toward the jar to retrieve the stick, they place it near the raised end again and repeat the movement.

A person folds the red printed sheet into a narrow rectangle and leaves it on the left of the small covered table. They lift and fold the cream knitted scarf into a compact bundle at the center. They then fold the white socks together and set them on the right, leaving a row of folded items behind the green vegetable, egg, and spoon.

The person lifts a dark garment from the pile on the left and folds it onto the right side of the table. They add the beige knitted garment, the pink garment, and another dark item in turn, lifting and folding each onto the growing stack. Finally, they fold the checked scarf into a compact rectangle and place it on top.

A seated person lifts a red printed garment, folds it and places it on the table. They fold a dark garment onto it, then add a pale patterned piece to the top of the pile. Finally, they pull a white paper towel toward the front, fold it into a smaller rectangle and smooth it down beside a pair of glasses.

Hands fold the sleeves and sides of a red shirt inward and turn it into a compact rectangle at one end of the table. They fold the gray trousers into a small bundle and place it beside the shirt. After briefly rubbing their palms, the person folds the printed sheet into a smaller rectangle, presses its creases and leaves it beneath the two folded garments.

A person folds a pink knitted garment into a pile on the table, then folds a gray garment and places it over the pink one. They briefly move the green knitwear aside while adding a dark navy garment to the stack. The green garment is folded and placed on top last, building a tall pile in front of the clear pitcher and fuzzy slippers.
